# Contract: Authentication System

*Generated by spec-writer. Hand edits are overwritten on regeneration.*

## Prerequisites

These conditions describe the environment in which items in this
contract are exercised. Producing them is part of the feature's
deliverable, alongside the implementation itself — a contract whose
prerequisites are not yet satisfied is not failing, it is still being
built. Once the feature is delivered, any missing condition halts item
execution until it is restored.

**Runtime services:**
- the backend HTTP service (`apps/backend`) is running, migrated against its PostgreSQL database, and reachable
- the `apps/web` Next.js application is running (dev server or production build) and reachable by a browser, with its proxy Route Handlers able to reach the backend service
- a browser (or browser-automation engine) is available to drive UI and E2E items

**Persistent state:**
- a user exists with name "Existing User", email "existing@example.com", and password "ValidPass123" (stored per this feature's own password-hashing rule), not suspended, not an admin. Used by: API-REGISTER-03, API-LOGIN-01, API-LOGIN-02, API-LOGOUT-01, UI-REGISTER-03, UI-LOGIN-01, UI-LOGIN-02, E2E-LOGIN-01, E2E-LOGOUT-01.

**Configuration:**
- the frontend recognizes a cookie named `videomax_session` (any non-empty value) as an "authenticated visitor" signal, the same placeholder contract this project's landing-page feature already established and this feature now formalizes with real issuance. Used by: UI-REGISTER-01, UI-LOGIN-01, UI-LOGOUT-01, E2E-REGISTER-01, E2E-LOGIN-01, E2E-LOGOUT-01.
- the backend's session-signing key is configured and stable for the duration of a run (sessions created before a key change cannot be resolved after it). Used by: every item that creates or resolves a session — all API, UI, and E2E items in this contract.
- the frontend's internal backend base URL is configured and points at the running backend service. Used by: every UI and E2E item, since all of them traverse the proxy Route Handlers.

## Quality gates

Each gate must pass for the feature to be considered ready.

- **Backend architecture audit** — `npm run gates` — the consolidated backend check (TypeScript compiles with no errors, ESLint reports no errors, dependency-cruiser reports no forbidden cross-layer imports, the structural architecture check passes, madge reports no circular imports, knip reports no orphaned files/exports) succeeds as a whole.
- **Backend tests** — `npm run test --workspace apps/backend` — the Vitest suite (domain, use case, and handler tests) passes.
- **Backend build** — `npm run build --workspace apps/backend` — the TypeScript production build completes without errors.
- **Frontend lint** — `npm run lint --workspace apps/web` — ESLint reports no errors across the frontend app.
- **Frontend typecheck** — `npm run typecheck --workspace apps/web` — TypeScript compiles with no type errors (`tsc --noEmit`).
- **Frontend unit/component tests** — `npm run test --workspace apps/web` — the Vitest + React Testing Library suite passes.
- **Frontend end-to-end tests** — `npm run test:e2e --workspace apps/web` — the Playwright suite passes against a running build.
- **Frontend build** — `npm run build --workspace apps/web` — the Next.js production build completes without errors.

## Coverage Manifest

| PRD Acceptance Criterion | Covered by |
|---|---|
| User can register with valid name, email, and password | API-REGISTER-01, UI-REGISTER-01, E2E-REGISTER-01 |
| Passwords shorter than 8 characters or missing a letter or number are rejected with inline messages | API-REGISTER-02, UI-REGISTER-02 |
| Duplicate email at registration returns a clear error | API-REGISTER-03, UI-REGISTER-03 |
| Login fails with a generic "Invalid email or password" message on wrong credentials | API-LOGIN-02, UI-LOGIN-02 |

| After successful registration the user is automatically logged in and lands on `/app` | UI-REGISTER-01, E2E-REGISTER-01 |
| Logout terminates the session and redirects to `/` | API-LOGOUT-01, UI-LOGOUT-01, E2E-LOGOUT-01 |

## HTTP API

**Verification mode:** Send an HTTP request to the running backend service; assert response status, headers, body, and any direct persisted side-effect.

### Register

**Common given:** the backend is running with default configuration.

#### `API-REGISTER-01` — happy path
- given: no user exists with email "newuser@example.com"
- when: POST /auth/register with body `{ name: "New User", email: "newuser@example.com", password: "ValidPass123" }`
- then:
  - response is `201` with body `{ user: { id, name: "New User", email: "newuser@example.com", isAdmin: false, createdAt }, sessionToken: non-empty }`
  - a user now exists with that email, a hashed password (never the plaintext value), `isAdmin: false`

#### `API-REGISTER-02` — weak password rejected
- given: no user exists with email "weakpass@example.com"
- when: POST /auth/register with body `{ name: "Weak Pass", email: "weakpass@example.com", password: "OnlyLetters" }` (no digit)
- then:
  - response is `422` with `code: "WEAK_PASSWORD"`
  - response `details.reasons` names the missing-number rule
  - no user is persisted with that email

#### `API-REGISTER-03` — duplicate email rejected
- given: (default), and a user already exists with email "existing@example.com"
- when: POST /auth/register with body `{ name: "Someone Else", email: "existing@example.com", password: "ValidPass123" }`
- then:
  - response is `409` with `code: "USER_ALREADY_EXISTS"`
  - the existing user's row (name, hashed password) is unchanged

### Login

**Common given:** a user exists with email "existing@example.com" and password "ValidPass123".

#### `API-LOGIN-01` — happy path
- given: (default)
- when: POST /auth/login with body `{ email: "existing@example.com", password: "ValidPass123" }`
- then:
  - response is `200` with body `{ user: { id, email: "existing@example.com" }, sessionToken: non-empty }`
  - the returned `sessionToken` resolves to an active session for that user (a subsequent `GET /auth/me` with it as the bearer token returns `200`)

#### `API-LOGIN-02` — wrong password rejected
- given: (default), and the supplied password is "WrongPass999"
- when: POST /auth/login with that password
- then:
  - response is `401` with `code: "UNAUTHENTICATED"` and message "Invalid email or password"
  - no session is created for that user

### Logout

**Common given:** a user exists with email "existing@example.com" and password "ValidPass123" and has an active session token from a prior login.

#### `API-LOGOUT-01` — logout invalidates the session
- given: (default)
- when: POST /auth/logout with header `Authorization: Bearer <that session's token>`
- then:
  - response is `204`
  - the same token no longer resolves to an active session (a subsequent `GET /auth/me` with it as the bearer token returns `401`)

## UI

**Verification mode:** Render the surface, drive it with user-like inputs (clicks, typing); assert observable surface state (DOM, visible text, navigation, cookies).

### Register

**Common given:** anonymous visitor (no `videomax_session` cookie) on `/register`.

#### `UI-REGISTER-01` — successful registration logs the user in and lands on /app
- given: (default), and no user exists with email "browser-newuser@example.com"
- when: fill name, email "browser-newuser@example.com", and a valid password, then submit the registration form
- then:
  - the browser ends up on `/app`
  - a `videomax_session` cookie is now present

#### `UI-REGISTER-02` — weak password shows an inline rule violation
- given: (default)
- when: fill a valid name and email but a password missing a digit, then submit
- then:
  - an inline message is shown naming the missing-number rule
  - the browser stays on `/register`

#### `UI-REGISTER-03` — duplicate email shows a clear inline error
- given: (default), and a user already exists with email "existing@example.com"
- when: fill the form with email "existing@example.com" and a valid password, then submit
- then:
  - an inline error is shown indicating an account with this email already exists
  - the browser stays on `/register`

### Login

**Common given:** a user exists with email "existing@example.com" and password "ValidPass123"; anonymous visitor on `/login`.

#### `UI-LOGIN-01` — successful login redirects to /app
- given: (default)
- when: fill email "existing@example.com" and password "ValidPass123", then submit
- then:
  - the browser ends up on `/app`
  - a `videomax_session` cookie is now present

#### `UI-LOGIN-02` — invalid credentials show a generic error
- given: (default), and the supplied password is "WrongPass999"
- when: fill the form with that password and submit
- then:
  - a generic "Invalid email or password" message is shown
  - the browser stays on `/login`

### Logout

#### `UI-LOGOUT-01` — logout terminates the session and redirects to /
- given: a user is logged in (a valid `videomax_session` cookie is present)
- when: click "Log out"
- then:
  - the browser ends up on `/`
  - the `videomax_session` cookie is no longer present

## E2E

**Verification mode:** Run the full system (frontend + backend + database); drive through a real browser; assert cross-stack behavior.

### Register

#### `E2E-REGISTER-01` — registration persists a real user and an authenticated session across reload
- given: no user exists with email "e2e-newuser@example.com"; anonymous visitor on `/register`
- when: complete the registration form with that email and a valid password, then reload the browser at `/app`
- then:
  - immediately after submission, the browser ends up on `/app`
  - after reload, `/app` still shows the registered user's name (the session persists across reload)
  - a user now exists in the database with that email

### Login

#### `E2E-LOGIN-01` — login persists an authenticated session across reload
- given: a user exists with email "existing@example.com" and password "ValidPass123"; anonymous visitor on `/login`
- when: submit those credentials, then reload the browser at `/app`
- then:
  - immediately after submission, the browser ends up on `/app`
  - after reload, `/app` still shows the logged-in user's name

### Logout

#### `E2E-LOGOUT-01` — logout invalidates the session at the database level
- given: a user exists with email "existing@example.com" and password "ValidPass123", logged in through `/login` so the browser's `videomax_session` cookie is backed by a real session row in the database
- when: click "Log out"
- then:
  - the browser ends up on `/`
  - the session row that backed that cookie's token no longer exists in the database
